edges.subject: CLN1
edges.quote: The CLN1 disease is a fatal neurodegenerative LSD, caused by inactivating mutations in the CLN1 gene encoding palmitoyl-protein thioesterase-1 (PPT1).

edges.subject: CLN1 disease
edges.quote: We previously reported that in Cln1-/- mice, which mimic human CLN1-disease, endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-stress leads to unfolded protein response (UPR) contributing to neurodegeneration.

edges.subject: CLN1 disease
edges.quote: We propose that impaired anterograde trafficking causes excessive accumulation of proteins in the ER causing ER-stress and UPR contributing to neurodegeneration in CLN1 disease.

edges.subject: S-palmitoylation
edges.quote: S-palmitoylation, a reversable posttranslational modification by saturated fatty acids (generally palmitate) facilitates endosomal trafficking of many proteins, especially in the brain.

edges.subject: ZDHHCs
edges.quote: While palmitoyl-acyltransferases (called ZDHHCs) catalyze S-palmitoylation, depalmitoylation is mediated by palmitoyl-protein thioesterases (PPTs).
